description: Comprehensive question bank on Tenses (English Grammar) for FDA & SDA Competitive Examinations. Based on 17.2 Tenses notes covering all 12 tense forms, structures, usage rules, conditionals, stative verbs, common errors, and irregular verbs.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is tense?

options.A: The grammatical form or construction of a verb that locates an action, event or state in time
options.B: The speed at which a sentence is spoken
options.C: The number of words in a sentence
options.D: The tone used in a question

questions.explanation: Tense is the grammatical form or construction of a verb that locates an action, event or state in time, or relates it to a reference time.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What are the three traditional time categories in English tense?
questions.explanation: The three traditional time categories are present, past and future.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What are the four aspects in the traditional tense system?

options.A: Simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous

questions.explanation: The four aspects are simple, continuous (progressive), perfect and perfect continuous (perfect progressive).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How many tense forms are taught in the traditional 12-tense system?
questions.explanation: Twelve forms are taught: four present, four past and four future forms.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does the simple aspect express?

options.A: Habits, facts, states, repeated actions or events viewed as a whole
options.B: An action in progress around a particular time
options.C: An action viewed in relation to a later reference point
options.D: The duration of an activity up to a reference point

questions.explanation: The simple aspect expresses habits, facts, states, repeated actions or events viewed as a whole.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does the continuous aspect express?

options.A: An action or situation in progress around a particular time, often temporary or ongoing
options.B: A completed action with present relevance
options.D: An action completed before another past action

questions.explanation: The continuous aspect expresses an action or situation in progress around a particular time, often temporary or ongoing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does the perfect aspect express?

options.A: An action or situation viewed in relation to a later reference point; it can show completion, experience or a result
options.B: An action in progress at a particular time
options.D: The duration of an activity up to a reference point

questions.explanation: The perfect aspect expresses an action or situation viewed in relation to a later reference point; it can show completion, experience or a result.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does the perfect continuous aspect express?

options.A: The duration or ongoing nature of an activity up to a reference point
options.B: A completed action with no connection to the present

questions.explanation: The perfect continuous aspect expresses the duration or ongoing nature of an activity up to a reference point.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is V1 in verb forms?

options.A: The base form: go, write, play
options.B: The simple past form: went, wrote, played
options.C: The past participle: gone, written, played

questions.explanation: V1 is the base form of the verb, such as go, write, play.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is V2 in verb forms?

options.A: The base form: go, write, play
options.B: The simple past form: went, wrote, played
options.C: The past participle: gone, written, played

questions.explanation: V2 is the simple past form of the verb, such as went, wrote, played.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is V3 in verb forms?

options.A: The base form: go, write, play
options.B: The simple past form: went, wrote, played
options.C: The past participle: gone, written, played

questions.explanation: V3 is the past participle form of the verb, such as gone, written, played.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is V-ing in verb forms?

options.A: The base form: go, write, play
options.B: The simple past form: went, wrote, played
options.C: The past participle: gone, written, played
options.D: The -ing form: going, writing, playing, used in continuous verb phrases

questions.explanation: V-ing is the -ing form of the verb, such as going, writing, playing; it is used in continuous verb phrases.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which auxiliary is used in continuous forms?

options.A: A form of be (am, is, are, was, were, been) + V-ing
options.B: A form of have (has, have, had) + V3
options.C: A form of do (do, does, did) + V1
options.D: A form of will (will, would) + V1

questions.explanation: Continuous forms use a form of be (am, is, are, was, were, been) + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which auxiliary is used in perfect forms?

options.A: A form of be (am, is, are, was, were, been) + V-ing
options.B: A form of have (has, have, had) + V3
options.C: A form of do (do, does, did) + V1
options.D: A form of will (will, would) + V1

questions.explanation: Perfect forms use a form of have (has, have, had) + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between tense and time?

options.A: Time is the real-world reference; tense is the grammatical form
options.B: Tense is the real-world reference; time is the grammatical form
options.C: They are exactly the same thing
options.D: Tense applies only to past; time applies only to future

questions.explanation: Time is the real-world reference; tense is the grammatical form. A present form can refer to future time: 'The train leaves tomorrow.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the simple present tense used for?

options.A: Habits, routines, facts, general truths, stable states, instructions and timetables
options.C: Actions completed before another past action
options.D: Actions in progress at a future time

questions.explanation: The simple present is used for habits, routines, facts, general truths, stable states, instructions and timetables.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the simple present tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the simple present is S + V1, adding -s/-es with a third-person singular subject.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the simple present tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the simple present is S + do/does not + V1.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the simple present tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the simple present is Do/Does + S + V1?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of simple present tense?
questions.explanation: 'She works' is an example of simple present tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the simple present tense?

options.A: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day
options.B: now, at the moment, currently, today
options.C: already, just, yet, ever, never, so far

questions.explanation: Common expressions with simple present include always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the present continuous tense used for?

options.A: Actions happening now; temporary situations; changing trends; definite personal arrangements
options.D: Actions completed before a future time

questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for actions happening now, temporary situations, changing trends and definite personal arrangements.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the present continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the present continuous is S + am/is/are + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the present continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the present continuous is S + am/is/are not + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the present continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the present continuous is Am/Is/Are + S + V-ing?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of present continuous tense?
questions.explanation: 'She is reading' is an example of present continuous tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the present continuous tense?

options.A: now, at the moment, currently, today

questions.explanation: Common expressions with present continuous include now, at the moment, currently, today. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the present perfect tense used for?

options.A: Past action with present relevance; life experience; recent completion; present result; state continuing to now
options.C: Completed past actions with no present relevance
options.D: Actions in progress at a past time

questions.explanation: The present perfect is used for past action with present relevance, life experience, recent completion, present result and state continuing to now.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the present perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the present perfect is S + has/have + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the present perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the present perfect is S + has/have not + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the present perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the present perfect is Has/Have + S + V3?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of present perfect tense?
questions.explanation: 'She has finished' is an example of present perfect tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the present perfect tense?

options.A: already, just, yet, ever, never, so far, since, for

questions.explanation: Common expressions with present perfect include already, just, yet, ever, never, so far, since, for. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the present perfect continuous tense used for?

options.A: Activity begun in the past and continuing now, or recently stopped with present evidence; emphasis on duration
options.B: Completed past actions with no present relevance
options.D: Actions completed before a future time

questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous is used for activity begun in the past and continuing now, or recently stopped with present evidence; it emphasizes duration.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the present perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the present perfect continuous is S + has/have been + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the present perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the present perfect continuous is S + has/have not been + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the present perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the present perfect continuous is Has/Have + S + been + V-ing?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of present perfect continuous tense?

options.A: She has been studying for two hours.
options.B: She has studied for two hours.
options.C: She is studying for two hours.

questions.explanation: 'She has been studying for two hours' is an example of present perfect continuous tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the present perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: Common expressions with present perfect continuous include for, since, all day, lately. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the simple past tense used for?

options.A: Completed past actions; past habits/states; sequence of past events
options.D: Actions in progress at a future time

questions.explanation: The simple past is used for completed past actions, past habits/states and a sequence of past events.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the simple past tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the simple past is S + V2.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the simple past tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the simple past is S + did not + V1.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the simple past tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the simple past is Did + S + V1?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of simple past tense?
questions.explanation: 'They visited Delhi' is an example of simple past tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the simple past tense?
questions.explanation: Common expressions with simple past include yesterday, last week, ago, in 2010. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the past continuous tense used for?

options.A: Action in progress at a past time; background action; interrupted or simultaneous actions

questions.explanation: The past continuous is used for an action in progress at a past time, a background action, and interrupted or simultaneous actions.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the past continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the past continuous is S + was/were + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the past continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the past continuous is S + was/were not + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the past continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the past continuous is Was/Were + S + V-ing?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of past continuous tense?

options.A: I was reading when he called.
options.C: I have read when he called.
options.D: I had read when he called.

questions.explanation: 'I was reading when he called' is an example of past continuous tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the past continuous tense?

options.A: while, as, at that time, yesterday at 8 p.m.

questions.explanation: Common expressions with past continuous include while, as, at that time, yesterday at 8 p.m. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the past perfect tense used for?

options.A: Action completed before another past action or past reference time
options.B: Action in progress at a past time
options.D: Action completed before a future time

questions.explanation: The past perfect is used for an action completed before another past action or past reference time.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the past perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the past perfect is S + had + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the past perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the past perfect is S + had not + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the past perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the past perfect is Had + S + V3?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of past perfect tense?

options.A: The train had left before we arrived.
options.B: The train left before we arrived.
options.C: The train has left before we arrived.
options.D: The train was leaving before we arrived.

questions.explanation: 'The train had left before we arrived' is an example of past perfect tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the past perfect tense?

options.A: before, after, by the time, already

questions.explanation: Common expressions with past perfect include before, after, by the time, already. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the past perfect continuous tense used for?

options.A: Activity continuing for a period before a past event; emphasis on duration or cause
options.B: Action completed before another past action
options.D: Action completed before a future time

questions.explanation: The past perfect continuous is used for an activity continuing for a period before a past event; it emphasizes duration or cause.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the past perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the past perfect continuous is S + had been + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the past perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The negative structure of the past perfect continuous is S + had not been + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the past perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the past perfect continuous is Had + S + been + V-ing?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of past perfect continuous tense?

options.A: He had been working for five hours.
options.B: He had worked for five hours.
options.C: He has been working for five hours.
options.D: He was working for five hours.

questions.explanation: 'He had been working for five hours' is an example of past perfect continuous tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the past perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: Common expressions with past perfect continuous include for, since, before, until. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the simple future tense used for?

options.A: Predictions, immediate decisions, promises, offers, willingness and future events

questions.explanation: The simple future is used for predictions, immediate decisions, promises, offers, willingness and future events.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the simple future tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the simple future is S + will + V1.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the simple future tense?

options.D: S + will not have been + V-ing

questions.explanation: The negative structure of the simple future is S + will not + V1.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the simple future tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the simple future is Will + S + V1?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of simple future tense?
questions.explanation: 'She will attend' is an example of simple future tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the simple future tense?
questions.explanation: Common expressions with simple future include tomorrow, next week, soon, later. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the future continuous tense used for?

options.A: Action in progress at a future time; expected activity; polite enquiry about plans
options.B: Action completed before a future time

questions.explanation: The future continuous is used for an action in progress at a future time, expected activity and polite enquiry about plans.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the future continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the future continuous is S + will be + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the future continuous tense?

options.D: S + will not have been + V-ing

questions.explanation: The negative structure of the future continuous is S + will not be + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the future continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the future continuous is Will + S + be + V-ing?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of future continuous tense?

options.A: I will be travelling at this time tomorrow.
options.B: I will travel at this time tomorrow.
options.C: I will have travelled at this time tomorrow.
options.D: I travelled at this time yesterday.

questions.explanation: 'I will be travelling at this time tomorrow' is an example of future continuous tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the future continuous tense?

options.A: this time tomorrow, at 8 p.m. tonight

questions.explanation: Common expressions with future continuous include this time tomorrow, at 8 p.m. tonight. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the future perfect tense used for?

options.A: Action completed before a specified future time or event
options.B: Action in progress at a future time
options.C: Duration of an activity up to a future point

questions.explanation: The future perfect is used for an action completed before a specified future time or event.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the future perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the future perfect is S + will have + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the future perfect tense?

options.D: S + will not have been + V-ing

questions.explanation: The negative structure of the future perfect is S + will not have + V3.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the future perfect tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the future perfect is Will + S + have + V3?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of future perfect tense?

options.A: She will have finished by June.
options.C: She will be finishing by June.

questions.explanation: 'She will have finished by June' is an example of future perfect tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the future perfect tense?

options.A: by, by then, by tomorrow, before

questions.explanation: Common expressions with future perfect include by, by then, by tomorrow, before. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the future perfect continuous tense used for?

options.A: Duration of an activity up to a future point; emphasis on how long it will have continued
options.B: Action completed before a future time
options.C: Action in progress at a future time

questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous is used for the duration of an activity up to a future point, emphasizing how long it will have continued.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the affirmative structure of the future perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The affirmative structure of the future perfect continuous is S + will have been + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the negative structure of the future perfect continuous tense?

options.A: S + will not have been + V-ing

questions.explanation: The negative structure of the future perfect continuous is S + will not have been + V-ing.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the interrogative structure of the future perfect continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The interrogative structure of the future perfect continuous is Will + S + have been + V-ing?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of future perfect continuous tense?

options.A: By December, she will have been teaching for ten years.
options.B: By December, she will have taught for ten years.
options.C: By December, she will be teaching for ten years.
options.D: By December, she has been teaching for ten years.

questions.explanation: 'By December, she will have been teaching for ten years' is an example of future perfect continuous tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which expressions are common with the future perfect continuous tense?

options.A: by then, by next month, for

questions.explanation: Common expressions with future perfect continuous include by then, by next month, for. They are clues, not absolute rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When is -s/-es added in the simple present?

options.A: With a third-person singular subject in an affirmative sentence
options.B: With all subjects in negative sentences

questions.explanation: -s/-es is added with a third-person singular subject in an affirmative sentence.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How are most verbs made third-person singular?
questions.explanation: Most verbs add -s to form the third-person singular: read-reads, play-plays.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How are verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x or -z commonly changed in the third-person singular?
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -ss, -x or -z commonly add -es: watch-watches, wash-washes, pass-passes, fix-fixes.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: How are consonant + y verbs changed in the third-person singular?

options.A: Change y to ies: study-studies, try-tries

questions.explanation: Consonant + y verbs change y to ies: study-studies, try-tries.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What are the present forms of be?

options.A: Am with I; is with he/she/it and singular nouns; are with you/we/they and plural nouns
options.B: Is with I; am with he/she/it; are with you/we/they
options.C: Are with I; is with you; am with they

questions.explanation: Present forms of be: am with I; is with he/she/it and singular nouns; are with you/we/they and plural nouns.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What are the third-person singular forms of have and do?
questions.explanation: The third-person singular forms of have and do are has and does.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which form follows do/does/did in negatives and questions?
questions.explanation: V1 follows do/does/did in negatives and questions: 'Does he work?'; 'Did she go?'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which form follows will?

options.A: V1: 'She will come,' not 'She will comes.'

questions.explanation: V1 follows will: 'She will come,' not 'She will comes.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which form follows has/have/had in perfect tenses?
questions.explanation: V3 follows has/have/had in perfect tenses: 'has written,' 'had gone.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which form follows be in continuous tenses?
questions.explanation: V-ing follows be in continuous tenses: 'is reading,' 'were playing.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which form follows been in perfect continuous tenses?
questions.explanation: V-ing follows been in perfect continuous tenses: 'has been working,' 'had been waiting.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between since and for?

options.A: Since identifies a starting point ('since Monday'); for identifies duration ('for three days')
options.B: Since identifies duration; for identifies a starting point
options.D: Since is used only with future; for only with past

questions.explanation: Since identifies a starting point ('since Monday'); for identifies duration ('for three days').

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between ago and before?

options.A: Ago measures backwards from now and is commonly used with simple past; before relates one event/time to another
options.B: Ago relates one event to another; before measures from now
options.D: Ago is used only with present perfect

questions.explanation: Ago measures backwards from now and is commonly used with simple past; before relates one event/time to another.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between during and for?

options.A: During is followed by an event/period noun ('during the meeting'); for is followed by a duration ('for two hours')
options.B: During is followed by a duration; for is followed by an event
options.D: During is used only in future tense

questions.explanation: During is followed by an event/period noun ('during the meeting'); for is followed by a duration ('for two hours').

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the difference between by and until?

options.A: By means no later than a deadline ('finish by six'); until means continuing up to a point ('wait until six')
options.B: By means continuing up to a point; until means no later than a deadline
options.D: By is used only with past tense

questions.explanation: By means no later than a deadline ('finish by six'); until means continuing up to a point ('wait until six').

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which tense is commonly used after when, before, after, until or as soon as for future time?

options.A: Simple present: 'I will call you when I arrive,' not ordinarily 'when I will arrive'

questions.explanation: Simple present is commonly used after when, before, after, until or as soon as for future time: 'I will call you when I arrive,' not ordinarily 'when I will arrive.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which tense is used in the ordinary if-clause of a first conditional?

options.A: Simple present: 'If she studies, she will pass.'
options.B: Simple future: 'If she will study, she will pass.'
options.C: Present perfect: 'If she has studied, she will pass.'
options.D: Past simple: 'If she studied, she will pass.'

questions.explanation: Simple present is used in the ordinary if-clause of a first conditional: 'If she studies, she will pass.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the first conditional structure?

options.A: If + simple present, will + V1; it expresses a real or possible future condition
options.C: If + past perfect, would have + V3

questions.explanation: The first conditional structure is If + simple present, will + V1; it expresses a real or possible future condition.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the second conditional structure?

options.A: If + simple past, would + V1; it expresses an unreal or unlikely present/future situation
options.C: If + past perfect, would have + V3

questions.explanation: The second conditional structure is If + simple past, would + V1; it expresses an unreal or unlikely present/future situation.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the third conditional structure?

options.A: If + past perfect, would have + V3; it expresses an unreal past condition

questions.explanation: The third conditional structure is If + past perfect, would have + V3; it expresses an unreal past condition.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What are stative verbs?

options.A: Verbs describing states, feelings, thoughts, possession or relationships: know, believe, understand, own, belong, love, prefer, need and seem
options.D: Verbs used only in the future tense

questions.explanation: Stative verbs describe states, feelings, thoughts, possession or relationships: know, believe, understand, own, belong, love, prefer, need and seem.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which tense is normally used with a stative verb describing a current state?

options.A: Simple present: 'I understand'; 'She owns a house.'

questions.explanation: Simple present is normally used with a stative verb describing a current state: 'I understand'; 'She owns a house.'

questions.subject: English
